philosophy.en: The program brings together fundamental and emerging knowledge in dermatology to train medical graduates with academic excellence and ethical values who contribute as much as they can to society.

title.th: การลงทะเบียนวิทยานิพนธ์

items.en: Students register for the thesis after at least 2 regular semesters of coursework, with at least 12 credits and a GPAX of 3.00 or higher.
items.th: ลงทะเบียนวิทยานิพนธ์ได้หลังเรียนรายวิชาอย่างน้อย 2 ภาคการศึกษาปกติ ได้อย่างน้อย 12 หน่วยกิต และมีคะแนนเฉลี่ยสะสมไม่ต่ำกว่า 3.00

items.en: The thesis is written and presented in English.
items.th: เขียนและนำเสนอวิทยานิพนธ์เป็นภาษาอังกฤษ

items.en: After registering, the student submits a proposal to the Dermatology Program Committee, and the Dean appoints an advisory and examination committee of at least 3 members to guide the student and run the proposal and final defense.
items.th: หลังลงทะเบียน นักศึกษาเสนอเค้าโครงต่อคณะกรรมการหลักสูตรตจวิทยา และคณบดีแต่งตั้งคณะกรรมการที่ปรึกษาและสอบวิทยานิพนธ์อย่างน้อย 3 คน เพื่อให้คำแนะนำและจัดสอบเค้าโครงและสอบป้องกัน

items.en: Thesis advisors meet the graduate program standards of the Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation (MHESI).
items.th: อาจารย์ที่ปรึกษามีคุณสมบัติตามเกณฑ์มาตรฐานหลักสูตรระดับบัณฑิตศึกษาของกระทรวงการอุดมศึกษา วิทยาศาสตร์ วิจัยและนวัตกรรม (อว.)

title.th: การสอบเค้าโครงวิทยานิพนธ์

items.en: The Dean appoints a committee of 3: the thesis advisor, a Thammasat University faculty member and an external expert. The advisor holds a doctorate or is at least an Associate Professor in the field.
items.th: คณบดีแต่งตั้งคณะกรรมการ 3 คน ได้แก่ อาจารย์ที่ปรึกษา อาจารย์มหาวิทยาลัยธรรมศาสตร์ และผู้ทรงคุณวุฒิภายนอก อาจารย์ที่ปรึกษาต้องมีวุฒิปริญญาเอกหรือดำรงตำแหน่งไม่ต่ำกว่ารองศาสตราจารย์ในสาขานั้น

items.en: The student registers for the thesis in the semester of the proposal exam and submits the proposal through the CICM Graduate Studies Program with the advisor's approval.

core.name: Responsible Research and Ethics in Bioclinical Sciences
core.desc: Introduction to responsible research; relevant information for initiating research; critical reading and analysis; guidelines for good practice, ethics and regulations in bioclinical sciences; responsible protocol writing; planning and setting up experiments and research; responsible peer review; good data management practice and quality standards; considerations for reports and publication; ethical issues in publication; and presentation of research results.

core.name: Statistical Methods in Bioclinical Sciences
core.desc: Principles and application of biostatistics to bioclinical research; types of variables and data; data presentation and summarization; population and sample; probability distributions; research and statistical hypotheses; estimation and hypothesis testing; parametric and non-parametric statistics; statistical tests for reliability and diagnosis; sample size estimation; and statistical software.

core.name: Clinical Dermatology I
core.desc: Structure of skin lesions and fundamentals of clinical diagnosis; clinical manifestations of common skin diseases and their pathogenesis, etiology, prognosis and management.

core.name: Dermatology Seminar
core.desc: Discussion of problems in patient care, clinical diagnosis, pathological diagnosis, laboratory investigation and treatment of chronic and rare skin diseases.

core.name: Dermatology Journal Club
core.desc: Formal presentation and discussion of current research in dermatological sciences and clinical dermatology by students, supervised by the course committee.

major.name: Dermatology Clinic I
major.desc: History taking and physical examination of outpatients; common dermatologic conditions and complicated skin diseases; symptoms and signs, laboratory investigations, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up, supervised by professors.

major.name: Basic Dermatology
major.desc: Structure and function of the skin; epidermis and keratinization; cell-cell adhesion, the epidermal-dermal junction and related diseases; dermis, fibroblasts and extracellular matrix proteins; eccrine and apocrine glands; melanocytes and pigmentation; subcutaneous fat and related diseases; biology of hair; biology of nails; photobiology and photoimmunology; photoprotection; principles of topical therapy; principles of systemic therapy and immunosuppressive medication; common investigations in dermatological practice.

major.name: Advanced Dermatology
major.desc: Innate and adaptive immunity in the skin; cytokines, chemokines and antigen-antibody reactions; humoral immunity and complement; production and activation of neutrophils and eosinophils; immunopathogenesis of atopic dermatitis and psoriasis; pruritus and neurobiology of the skin; biologic drugs and targeted therapy; stem cells and basic signaling pathways in the skin; in vitro and in vivo models for investigative dermatology.

major.name: Dermatopathology
major.desc: Histopathological examination and interpretation of skin diseases.

major.name: Investigations in Dermatology
major.desc: Principles of molecular biology techniques; dermoscopy of skin conditions and hair; skin and soft tissue imaging; bioinformatics in dermatology; AI in dermatology; bio-based materials in dermatology and cosmetology; cell-based therapy; exosomes; teledermatology; how to generate good research; systematic review and meta-analysis; clinic operating systems; healthcare communication and public speaking.

major.name: Clinical Dermatology II
major.desc: Structure of skin lesions and fundamentals of clinical diagnosis; clinical manifestations of complicated skin diseases.

major.name: Dermatology Clinic II
major.desc: History taking and physical examination of outpatients; common dermatologic conditions and complicated skin diseases; symptoms and signs, laboratory investigations, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up, supervised by professors.

major.name: Dermatosurgery
major.desc: Treatment of skin diseases, aging skin and skin tumors by surgery and laser; excision and repair; electrosurgery; cryosurgery; ablative laser and chemical peels; non-ablative laser and light therapy; botulinum toxin and soft tissue augmentation; vascular laser and treatment of varicose veins; cosmetic and skin care in dermatology, supervised by professors.

major.name: Hands-on Experiences in Dermatology
major.desc: Practice in dermatological procedures: fruit lab and biopsy, cadaver workshop, laser and injection. The clinical track grades it on an average score; the cosmetic track grades it P (pass) or N (not pass) with no credits.

elective.name: Dermatological Practice I
elective.desc: Outpatient observation abroad; history taking and physical examination; common, complicated, rare and endemic skin diseases; symptoms and signs, laboratory investigations, interpretation, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up, supervised by a professor.

elective.name: Dermatological Practice II
elective.desc: Outpatient observation abroad; history taking and physical examination; common, complicated, rare and endemic skin diseases; symptoms and signs, laboratory investigations, interpretation, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up, supervised by a professor.

elective.name: Laser and Injection
elective.desc: Aesthetic treatment with current equipment and technology, from basic principles and clinical use to preventing and treating complications; laser, radiofrequency and other devices for pigmentary disorders, tattoos, hair loss, acne, scars, photoaging, wrinkles and hair removal.

thesis.name: Thesis
thesis.desc: Literature review, a research outline and systematic research that creates new knowledge in dermatology, with research ethics; writing the thesis; presenting results and preparing articles for publication; ethics in publishing, under the thesis advisory committee.

required.name: Responsible Research and Ethics in Bioclinical Sciences
required.desc: Introduction to responsible research; relevant information for initiating research; critical reading and analysis; guidelines for good practice, ethics and regulations in bioclinical sciences; responsible protocol writing; planning and setting up experiments and research; responsible peer review; good data management practice and quality standards; considerations for reports and publication; ethical issues in publication; and presentation of research results.

required.name: Statistical Methods in Bioclinical Sciences
required.desc: Principles and application of biostatistics to bioclinical research; types of variables and data; data presentation and summarization; population and sample; probability distributions; research and statistical hypotheses; estimation and hypothesis testing; parametric and non-parametric statistics; statistical tests for reliability and diagnosis; sample size estimation; and statistical software.

required.name: Clinical Dermatology I
required.desc: Structure and morphology of skin lesions and principles of clinical diagnosis; clinical manifestations, pathogenesis, etiology, prognosis and management of common skin disorders; principles of clinical dermatology and topical therapy; papulosquamous and vesiculobullous disorders; drug eruptions and dermatological emergencies; eczema and dermatitis; acne, rosacea and adnexal disorders; urticaria and angioedema; hair and nail disorders; pigmentary disorders; cutaneous vasculopathies; benign and malignant skin tumors; bacterial, viral, fungal and tropical dermatoses.

required.name: Dermatology Seminar
required.desc: Discussion of clinical problems in patient care, clinical and pathological diagnosis, laboratory investigations and the management of chronic and rare skin disorders.

required.name: Dermatology Journal Club
required.desc: Formal presentation and discussion of current research in dermatological sciences and clinical dermatology under the course committee, and presentation of research progress.

required.name: Dermatology Clinic I
required.desc: History taking and physical examination of outpatients; clinical evaluation of common and complicated skin conditions; signs and symptoms; laboratory investigations; diagnosis; treatment; and follow-up, supervised by faculty members.

required.name: Basic Dermatology
required.desc: Development and structure of the epidermis; keratinocyte kinetics and differentiation; epidermal lipids; DNA repair and carcinogenesis; the dermoepidermal junction and basement membrane zone and blistering disorders; collagen, elastin, ground substance and fibroblasts; wound healing; nutrition and the skin; percutaneous absorption and thermoregulation; the sebaceous unit; apocrine and eccrine sweat glands; hair biology; nail structure and growth; inflammation and inflammatory mediators; hormone receptors in the skin; and cutaneous stem cells.

required.name: Advanced Dermatology
required.desc: Innate and adaptive immunity in the skin; cytokines and chemokines; humoral immunity and complement; neutrophil and eosinophil production and activation; common signaling pathways; carcinogenesis; immunopathogenesis of atopic dermatitis, contact dermatitis, psoriasis, blistering diseases, acne vulgaris, urticaria, graft-versus-host disease, lichen planus and alopecia areata; immunosuppressive and biologic therapy; cutaneous thermoregulation; neurobiology and hormonal regulation of the skin; cosmeceuticals; and innovations in skin technology.

required.name: Dermatopathology
required.desc: Histopathological examination and interpretation of skin diseases.

required.name: Investigations in Dermatology
required.desc: Common laboratory investigations in dermatology; dermoscopy; allergy testing; phototesting; cell culture; protein and RNA extraction and quantification; mRNA quantification and PCR; immunohistochemical staining; immunofluorescence; and principles of drug development in dermatology, supervised by faculty members.

required.name: Clinical Dermatology II
required.desc: Clinical manifestations, pathogenesis, etiology, prognosis and management of common and complex skin disorders: contact dermatitis; photodermatoses; pediatric dermatology; skin disorders of pregnancy and aging; non-infectious inflammatory dermatoses; skin signs of systemic disease; autoimmune connective tissue diseases; leprosy and mycobacterial infections; sexually transmitted diseases and HIV; orogenital disorders; dermal and subcutaneous disorders; genodermatoses; systemic therapy; photoprotection; complementary and alternative therapy. Requires CMD 601.

required.name: Dermatology Clinic II
required.desc: History taking and physical examination of outpatients; clinical evaluation of common and complex skin conditions; signs and symptoms; laboratory investigations; diagnosis; treatment; and follow-up, supervised by faculty members.

required.name: Dermatosurgery
required.desc: Surgical and laser treatment of skin diseases, skin aging and skin tumors; excision and repair; electrosurgery; cryosurgery; ablative laser and chemical peels; non-ablative laser and light therapy; botulinum toxin and soft tissue augmentation; vascular laser and varicose veins; cosmetic and skin care in dermatology, supervised by faculty members.

elective.name: Dermatological Practice I
elective.desc: Outpatient observation abroad; history taking and physical examination; common, complicated, rare and endemic skin diseases; symptoms and signs, laboratory investigations, interpretation, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up, supervised by a professor.

elective.name: Dermatological Practice II
elective.desc: Outpatient observation abroad; history taking and physical examination; common, complicated, rare and endemic skin diseases; symptoms and signs, laboratory investigations, interpretation, diagnosis, treatment and follow-up, supervised by a professor.

elective.name: Clinical Drug Development
elective.desc: Key elements of a clinical study: quality standards and regulations such as GMP, GCLP and GCP, audits and inspections; the clinical protocol; case report forms; the investigator brochure; informed consent; ethics committees and institutional review boards; source document verification; monitoring visits; drug accountability; laboratory and clinical supplies; and adverse events.

elective.name: Current Concepts in Dermatological Drug Discovery and Development
elective.desc: How dermatological drugs are discovered and developed: target identification; pre-clinical studies; chemistry, manufacturing and control (CMC); clinical development phases I to IV; pharmacokinetics, toxicokinetics and pharmacogenomics; and regulatory requirements.

elective.name: Techniques in Dermatological Drug Research and Development
elective.desc: Chemical and physical stability testing; in vitro and in vivo models of skin penetration and absorption; in vitro and in vivo models of dermal toxicity and efficacy; and non-invasive bioengineering techniques.

elective.name: Research Protocol Design
elective.desc: Writing a research protocol: background, literature review, research questions and hypotheses; study design, site, population, sample size, sampling, instruments, procedures and data analysis; ethics; timeline, budget and logistics; and publishing the results.

dissertation.name: Dissertation
dissertation.desc: A research proposal in bioclinical sciences; research that creates new knowledge or innovation; writing the dissertation; preparing manuscripts for publication; research and publishing ethics. Registered as CMD 900, CMD 901 or CMD 902 by study plan.

noncredit.name: Dermatology Journal Seminar
noncredit.desc: Graded P (pass) or N (not pass), no credits.

noncredit.name: Clinical Dermatology I
noncredit.desc: Graded P (pass) or N (not pass), no credits.

noncredit.desc: Graded P (pass) or N (not pass), no credits.

title.th: การลงทะเบียนดุษฎีนิพนธ์

items.en: Plan 1: from the first semester, once the student meets the program's requirements and has passed the qualifying examination.
items.th: แผน 1 ลงทะเบียนได้ตั้งแต่ภาคการศึกษาแรก เมื่อมีคุณสมบัติครบตามหลักสูตรและสอบผ่านการสอบวัดคุณสมบัติ

items.en: Plan 2: after at least one regular semester with 14 credits of required courses, a GPAX of 3.00 or higher, and a pass in the qualifying examination.
items.th: แผน 2 ลงทะเบียนได้หลังเรียนอย่างน้อย 1 ภาคการศึกษาปกติ ผ่านวิชาบังคับอย่างน้อย 14 หน่วยกิต คะแนนเฉลี่ยสะสมไม่ต่ำกว่า 3.00 และสอบผ่านการสอบวัดคุณสมบัติ

items.en: The dissertation is written in English.
items.th: เขียนดุษฎีนิพนธ์เป็นภาษาอังกฤษ

items.en: After registering, the student submits a proposal, and the Dean appoints an advisor and a dissertation committee of at least 5 members to guide the student and run the proposal and final examinations.
items.th: หลังลงทะเบียน นักศึกษาเสนอเค้าโครง และคณบดีแต่งตั้งอาจารย์ที่ปรึกษาและคณะกรรมการดุษฎีนิพนธ์อย่างน้อย 5 คน เพื่อให้คำแนะนำและจัดสอบเค้าโครงและสอบปากเปล่าขั้นสุดท้าย

title.th: การสอบดุษฎีนิพนธ์

items.en: The student registers for the full dissertation credits in the semester of the examination.
items.th: ลงทะเบียนดุษฎีนิพนธ์ครบจำนวนหน่วยกิตในภาคการศึกษาที่ขอสอบ

items.en: The examination comes after a pass in the English examination. Native English speakers and graduates of an English-medium program within two years of applying are exempt.
items.th: สอบได้หลังสอบผ่านภาษาอังกฤษ ผู้ที่ใช้ภาษาอังกฤษเป็นภาษาราชการและผู้สำเร็จหลักสูตรที่สอนเป็นภาษาอังกฤษภายใน 2 ปีก่อนวันสมัครได้รับการยกเว้น

items.en: The committee has at least 5 members, faculty and external experts, chaired by an external expert.
items.th: คณะกรรมการสอบมีอย่างน้อย 5 คน ประกอบด้วยอาจารย์ประจำหลักสูตรและผู้ทรงคุณวุฒิภายนอก โดยประธานเป็นผู้ทรงคุณวุฒิภายนอก

items.en: The examination is open to the public.
items.th: การสอบเปิดให้บุคคลทั่วไปเข้าฟังได้

items.en: An S (satisfactory) grade needs a unanimous decision of the committee.
items.th: ได้ระดับ S (ผ่าน) เมื่อคณะกรรมการมีมติเป็นเอกฉันท์

title.th: การสอบวัดคุณสมบัติ

items.en: Written and oral, run by the CICM Graduate Program twice each academic year.
items.th: สอบข้อเขียนและสอบปากเปล่า จัดโดยฝ่ายบัณฑิตศึกษา CICM ปีการศึกษาละ 2 ครั้ง

items.en: Students can apply from their first semester and must apply within 4 to 6 regular semesters of enrolling.
items.th: สมัครสอบได้ตั้งแต่ภาคการศึกษาแรก และต้องสมัครภายใน 4 ถึง 6 ภาคการศึกษาปกตินับจากวันเข้าศึกษา

items.en: Students must pass within two consecutive attempts or lose their student status.
items.th: ต้องสอบผ่านภายใน 2 ครั้งติดต่อกัน มิฉะนั้นพ้นสภาพนักศึกษา

items.en: A pass is needed before the dissertation proposal examination.
items.th: ต้องสอบผ่านก่อนสอบเค้าโครงดุษฎีนิพนธ์

quality.en: Course coordinators teach to the approved syllabus and give students the outline, activities and assessment at the start of each course. Sessions are recorded for review, and students use Moodle and V-Cube to reach classmates and instructors at any time.
quality.th: ผู้ประสานงานรายวิชาสอนตามประมวลรายวิชาที่ได้รับอนุมัติ และแจ้งเค้าโครง กิจกรรม และการประเมินผลเมื่อเริ่มรายวิชา การสอนมีการบันทึกเพื่อทบทวนคุณภาพ และนักศึกษาใช้ Moodle และ V-Cube ติดต่อเพื่อนและอาจารย์ได้ทุกเวลา
